stem: In a circle M of radius 5 cm, the chord AB = 7 cm and the chord CD = $X + 1$ cm. CD is closer to the centre than AB (MF < ME). Mark on the number line all the possible values of $X$, setting each end hollow (excluded) or filled (included).
solution: Radius = 5 cm, so the diameter is 10 cm; AB = 7 cm.
MF < ME, so CD is closer to the centre than AB, so CD is longer: $X + 1 > 7$, i.e. $X > 6$.
CD is a chord, so it is at most the diameter: $X + 1 \le 10$, so $X \le 9$.
So $X \in (6, 9]$, i.e. $6 < X \le 9$: hollow circle at 6, filled circle at 9, shaded between.

hints.text: Ask whether a chord can be exactly as long as the diameter, and whether CD can be exactly as long as AB when it is closer to the centre.
The closer a chord is to the centre, the longer it is. Compare CD with AB first, then with the longest chord of the circle, and remember CD is $X + 1$, not $X$.

notes: The completion-style blanks become the final interval; the figure's data is stated in the stem.
